nodes.label: README.md: Run the demo
nodes.description:
## Run the demo

Requires Node.js 24+ and npm.

```sh
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
npm start
```

Open [the local demo](http://127.0.0.1:3000). Enter `ADMIN_TOKEN` from your local `.env` into the panel. Replace the example token with a long random value before sharing a test environment. If `.env` is absent, the server generates and prints a temporary panel key for loopback use.

Choose **English** in the header to test the UI and chat in English. Spanish is the default; your explicit language preference is remembered in this browser. English commands: `hello`, `menu`, `cart`, `remove 1`, `clear`, `confirm`, `new`. Changing languages preserves your cart. In a real WhatsApp test conversation, send `English` or `Español` to choose the language.

1. Send `hola` in the chat simulator. Any initial text displays the menu.
2. Send `1 x 2`, then `3`: two completos and one limonada total **CLP 11,500**.
3. Send `confirmar`. Review the total and the explicitly simulated payment reference.
4. In the pickup dashboard, click **Simular pago y enviar a cocina**.
5. Mark the order ready, then confirm pickup. The dashboard updates counts and paid revenue.
6. Send `nuevo` to start another order after payment. Cart commands include `carrito`, `quitar 1`, and `vaciar` before confirmation.

The simulation payment reference points to the panel; it is not a hosted checkout and cannot charge a card. The panel button is the only simulation payment control. Refresh the operations panel to see orders received through the real WhatsApp test transport.

Set `POS_PROVIDER=toteat` (default) or `fudo` in `.env` to choose the simulated provider label. Both real adapters require provider access and implementation in #13/#22/#23. If port 3000 is occupied, set `PORT=3311` and open that port instead.

## Access package for the owner and restaurant partner

Prepare this information without sending a vendor request or creating an account:

1. Name the consenting restaurant, operational owner, selected provider, isolated test branch and permitted test window. Confirm who may inspect the kitchen and authorize synthetic orders. Do not use customer data for this exercise.
2. Obtain current authorized technical documentation, a definite test base URL, supported API version, allowed routes, rate limits and credential scope. Store credentials through approved secret configuration, outside Git, logs, fixtures and issue comments.
3. For Toteat, confirm API enablement, restaurant/local/user identifiers, external-order/origin configuration and shift rules against its configuration guide. Confirm the usable base URL: the recorded specification contains differing descriptive and `servers` URLs.
4. For Fudo, confirm external-order approval and Delivery availability. Obtain that integration's Client ID/Client Secret and approved contract. General/Pro API keys do not establish external-order permission; confirm any separate catalog requirement before purchasing or granting extra access.
5. Request sanitized examples of success, validation/authentication rejection, rate limiting, server failure, closed shift and timeout/status lookup. Ask which identifiers are stable correlation keys and which operations can charge or resend an order.
6. Confirm payment-method mapping, tax/tip/service assumptions and the settlement recipient. An order marked paid inside a POS is not evidence that a gateway settled money. Use authorized sandbox evidence before a real-money pilot.

These are preparation questions, not instructions to contact vendors, accept terms, purchase a plan or provision a merchant account. Those actions retain the documented owner and provider gates.

nodes.description:
## Data integrity and unit of work

Migration `001_restaurant_storage.sql` creates tenants/branches, users/memberships/tokens, sender mappings, products, conversations, orders/immutable line snapshots, simulation payment attempts, inbox replies, outbox state events, delivery receipts and audit events. Tenant-and-branch composite keys/FKs prevent cross-scope order/session/product references. Tokens have a unique digest and provider references are unique within their account scope.

The repository authenticates staff into a server-derived scope. Webhooks authenticate exact raw bytes first and then resolve the configured receiving phone ID through `channel_accounts`. Customer text, body properties, query parameters and `X-Tenant-ID` cannot select a restaurant. Unknown JSON properties are rejected rather than silently stripped.

Each unit of work uses one checked-out PostgreSQL client for `BEGIN` through `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, following [node-postgres transaction guidance](https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions). It locks the branch row before loading that branch's working set, as described by [PostgreSQL row-lock semantics](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/explicit-locking.html). This serializes concurrent app instances for the small POC without relying on an in-process mutex. Queries are parameterized, all domain reads/writes include tenant/branch scope, and save rejects changes to the transaction's scope or confirmed line/amount/provider snapshot.

The domain's Maps are transaction-local working sets in PostgreSQL mode. The database is the durable source; nothing from a previous request is required to reconstruct the next. Persisted inbox replies prevent repeated messages from adding items again after restart. Payment/POS references survive restart. State changes enqueue uniquely keyed outbox records in the same transaction, and mutations append an audit record with actor/action and scope. Audits do not contain message bodies, tokens or phone numbers.

This deliberately loads/saves one branch's small dataset per operation and uses a branch-level lock. It prioritizes correctness for the initial pilot; it is not suitable for unlimited order history/high throughput. Before increasing scale, replace bulk hydration with bounded per-aggregate queries and narrower locking while retaining the same isolation tests. Database RLS is not enabled; isolation currently relies on the authenticated repository boundary plus composite constraints. Use separate migration/admin and least-privilege application database users before staging customer data.

Use up to 3–4 implementation agents when available, plus the orchestrator/reviewer if the host supports it. Scale down to actual capacity. Give each agent a bounded outcome, owned paths, source/issue references, invariants and verification commands. Ask for a commit/diff, tests and unresolved assumptions. Agents may report progress to the orchestrator through supported collaboration tools; this does not authorize contacting third parties.

| Workstream | Scope and issues | Completion evidence now | External acceptance later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Messaging reliability / staff handoff | #10–#12: delivery callbacks, unknown-media/status batches, retention policy, dead-letter/recovery UX, permitted ready notifications, human help | Signed callback fixtures, state-ordering/replay/failure tests, auth/isolation, ES/EN staff flows; no blind resend of unknown outcomes | Approved recipient and actual phone journey; approved utility template outside service window |
| Checkout / financial orchestration | #8/#14/#15/#17 and local slice #27: durable attempts, separate financial/fulfillment states, Webpay sandbox adapter, cancellation/late payment/reconciliation | Mock gateway tests, immutable total checks, duplicate callbacks, concurrent workers, unknown outcomes, safe cash-vs-online choices, clear sandbox UI | Reachable hosted sandbox; merchant settlement/refund contract for real money |
| POS contract readiness | #2/#3/#7/#13/#16/#22/#23: Toteat/Fudo capability matrix, adapters where contract is known, synthetic harness and fail-closed configuration | Two isolated provider configurations, routing/mapping/error tests, exact evidence labels and access checklist | Approved accounts/contracts and real kitchen confirmation in each provider |
| Demo / deployment / operations | #18–#21/#27: bilingual dashboard/recovery, staging recipe, local acceptance scripts, privacy/runbooks and customer feedback kit | Reproducible build, isolated PG tests, keyboard/mobile ES/EN rehearsal, deployment/rollback checks without paid provisioning | Restaurant ownership/sign-off, cloud/budget authorization, real traffic go/no-go |

Allocate migrations and shared contracts to one owner at a time. Reserve migration numbers centrally. Sequence changes to `domain.ts`, `database.ts`, `app.ts` and `contracts.ts`; independent agents should not concurrently rewrite them. Use an integration branch with exclusive file ownership in this isolated cloud checkout, or sequential cherry-picks; never use shared uncoordinated edits. Do not create worktrees during cloud setup unless explicitly requested. Re-run the relevant integration suite after combining changes. A reviewer should examine payment authority, tenant isolation, message/order duplication, unknown outcomes and truthful statuses.

Recommended order: finish messaging recovery/status handling and financial state contracts; implement independent sandbox checkout; add ready notifications and staff exception flows; prepare staging and scripted bilingual rehearsal; continue POS readiness concurrently without claiming vendor acceptance. M0–M4 are outcome groups, not a requirement to finish all vendor approvals before writing independent code. #27 is the first standalone demo target; #21/#23 contain later restaurant/both-provider gates.

The official WhatsApp Business Tools MCP was configured and OAuth login succeeded on the founder's desktop; a business-list call verified access.

The founder says legal company registration is pending and explicitly defers business verification. Do not invent legal/tax/address details, submit verification, buy a subscription, or migrate/deregister the existing mobile number.

Do not assume an unverified business necessarily prevents every test-sender operation. Recheck actual account eligibility, profile prerequisites and the specific console/API response. Use the test sender if legitimately supported. Respect a genuine prerequisite error; continue fake-transport development independently. Recipient verification, a real inbound/outbound ordering loop, public webhook subscription and ready notifications have **not** been proved.

Official MCP guide: `https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp/whatsapp-business-tools-mcp`; endpoint `https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools` (Streamable HTTP + OAuth). It manages/debugs developer assets; the product runtime calls Cloud API directly. Follow the connected MCP's business-picker rules: list businesses first, show results and obtain an explicit selection even if one exists; inspect profile prerequisites before onboarding. Never auto-select assets or automatically grant broad permissions.

A cloud worker does not inherit desktop browser cookies, temporary tokens, OAuth/keychain storage, Codex user configuration, localhost callbacks or MCP registrations. Discover its actual tools; ask the owner to reconnect only when needed. Store runtime secrets in the cloud environment's secret facility, never in Git/graphs/issues/chat. The founder prefers to personally accept terms and complete password/OTP/CAPTCHA/security-sensitive grants. Do not request passwords in chat.
